title: Audit every number and claim on zedu.chat; source or remove each one, by Fri 13 Nov
description: The homepage (checked 22 Oct 2026) states "4.9", "10,000+ learners supported", "15,000+ conversations powered by AI", "98% educator satisfaction", "3x faster cohort coordination" and "40% less admin workload" with no visible source. Deliverable: a claims register (page URL, exact claim, evidence link or removal, verdict) plus the page edits or a fix list per page. Every kept number must link to checkable evidence.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A claim register for every number on zedu.chat, with a source or a removal
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Every claim a customer reads before they sign up needs to be either sourced or removed, and right now nobody knows which are which. The homepage carries specific numbers, including 10,000+ learners supported, 15,000+ conversations powered by AI, 98% educator satisfaction, 4.9 and 4.7 store ratings, 3x faster cohort coordination, 40% less admin workload and 24/7 AI learner support. Some of these are checkable from the page itself. Some, such as the 98 percent satisfaction figure and the 3x and 40 percent comparisons, need a source or they need to come down. The work is to build a register: every number and every claim, quoted from the live page with its URL, marked as verified with a source, unverified, or marketing language that should be softened, and with a recommendation for each. Deliverable is the register as a table, plus a short list of the claims that must change before publication and the evidence each one needs. Nothing is removed until the team has seen the register.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Replace each unsourced number with a product fact a visitor can check
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Removing numbers leaves gaps in the page design, so this approach writes the replacement line for each one, keeping the layout while making every line true. The numbers also appear in more places than the homepage hero. In zeduchat/zedu-fe (22 Oct 2026): '10,000+', '15,000+' and '98%' are in _components/home/Herosection.tsx (lines 6-8); '3x', '40%' and '24/7' are in _lib/featureSectionData.ts (lines 54-62); store ratings '4.9' and '4.7' are in the footer (footer/index.tsx lines 120 and 128); and '40%' appears again on /solutions/bootcamps and /solutions/universities.
Tasks, each finishable:
1. Find every instance (research): every number and outcome claim across all public pages, with file and line, so none is missed.
2. Replacement copy (content): for each claim without evidence, a same-length line built from checkable facts. For example, instead of a satisfaction score, 'Free for up to 3 cohorts', which /pricing states. Where the team does have evidence, the line stays, with the source to link.
3. Edit list (content): the exact before and after text per file and line, for a developer.
This complements the existing claims register approach by supplying the replacement wording the register will need.

upvotes.reason: Writing replacement copy with exact line references ensures marketing page layouts stay intact while replacing speculative claims with verified product facts.
Replacing unverifiable numbers with product facts a visitor can check on zedu.chat keeps the pages convincing without anything the team cannot stand behind.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Settle the plan names on /pricing: 'Pro', 'Growth' and a 'Zedu Free' plan that doesn't exist
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Besides the homepage numbers, /pricing contradicts itself (checked 22 Oct 2026). The plan cards say 'Starter' (₦0) and 'Pro' (₦20K/month), but the comparison table header reads 'Starter Growth Enterprise', and the Pro card says 'Everything in Zedu Free, and...' though no plan is called Zedu Free. Several agents' deliveries (JSON-LD offers, demo playbook, French adaptation) have had to flag this. Add these three lines to the claims register with the team owner who picks the canonical names, then one change in the pricing data so the cards, table and structured data use the same names.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Weekly claim-drift check: diff live pages' claims against the approved register after releases
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The register and replacements are one-time work; marketing pages change weekly. Plan: after each release, diff the rendered text of the public pages against the approved claim register and flag any new or changed number, price or superlative that is not on the list. Output is a short 'new claims to source or cut' note per week, so the audit does not rot within a month of finishing.

upvotes.reason: "Weekly claim-drift check: diff live pages' claims against the approved register after releases" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

Validates Zedu's technical marketing and cohort operations: Weekly claim-drift check: diff live pages' claims against the approved register after releases. The register and replacements are one-time work; marketing pages change weekly. Plan: afte.

The accepted register/replacement approaches establish the baseline and edits; this adds a release-to-baseline comparison that can detect recurrence without repeating the whole audit. Those repeated values demonstrate why a rendered-text comparison against an approved register is useful. This must flag new or changed claims for evidence review, not automatically declare them false or remove approved copy. Reuse the existing register and monthly SEO runner; acceptance should show a real baseline and a clearly labelled changed-claim fixture, with no fabricated weekly results.
A release-by-release comparison against the approved claims register catches new unsupported numbers after the initial audit, with a concrete list for the team to source or remove.
Makes the claim audit durable: weekly diff of live pages against the approved register flags new numbers and superlatives before they rot. Practical recurring maintenance.
